source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Restrict potassium and phosphorus to the same low targets for every person with CKD regardless of laboratory results or disease stage.","B":"Increase protein substantially for every person with CKD, including people who are not receiving dialysis or losing protein.","C":"Avoid nutrition modifications because dietary sodium, potassium, phosphorus, protein, and fluid intake do not affect CKD management.","D":"Individualize sodium, potassium, phosphorus, protein, and fluid goals to CKD stage, laboratory results, treatment status, and nutrition needs."}}
source_row.rationale: NIDDK explains that there is no single eating plan for all adults with CKD; sodium, potassium, phosphorus, protein and fluid goals are individualized as kidney function, laboratory values and treatment needs change.
source_row.source_detail: Why is healthy eating important if I have CKD?; How can I eat healthy with CKD?; nutrient-specific sections on sodium, potassium, phosphorus, protein and liquids. source_row.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease asks whether everyone with CKD should follow the same low-potassium, low-phosphorus, high-protein diet. Which response is best?
